data.name: Kran
data.gender_notes: Kran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kran is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kra', which means 'to move'. In Hindu mythology, Kran is the name of a demon king who was powerful and fierce. This name is bestowed upon boys to instill courage and strength. The name Kran carries the meaning “Bold, Strong” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kran usually hope their child will grow to embody bold, strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kran belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bold, Strong.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kran total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rama is popular in Hinduism and carries significant cultural significance. 'Rama' was the name of a great Hindu king and the central character of the epic 'Ramayana'. He is considered an ideal man and a perfect example of virtue, wisdom, courage, and righteousness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rama invokes divine qualities and represents the spiritual ideal of an enlightened being, embodying conditions of peace, harmony, and happiness in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kran: The divine messenger, carrying the wisdom of the cosmos in his heart, symbolizes the inner voice guiding us towards the path of truth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: The Puranic legend describes Kran as the king of the serpents and a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. He is also known as Anantha, Vasuki, and Shesha. Kran is considered to be the protector of the universe and is often depicted as coiling around the cosmic ocean. He is also believed to be the king of the underworld, and his common epithet, 'Kala', signifies time.

Another reference to Kran is found in the Mahabharata, where he is mentioned as the king of the serpents and the one who assumes the form of the demon Kaliya to torment the Yadavas. Kran is also the one who later saves the Yadavas by slaying Kaliya and is hailed as a hero by them.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Kran continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
